transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Um, I'm here because I just can't stop focusing on my face. Specifically, the left side of my face looks really uneven and puffy to me. 

I notice it constantly, especially on video calls for work, and in photos from my salsa classes. The thing is, everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything wrong or that they don't know what I'm talking about, but I just can't stop looking at it. It's... well, it's really starting to mess with my work and my social life, so I figured I needed to talk to someone about it.

When people tell you they don't see what you see, do you ever consider the possibility that your perception of your face might be inaccurate, or are you completely certain that the puffiness and unevenness are objectively there?

I mean... I guess it's a little bit of both. When I look at myself, I am completely certain it's there. It just looks so obvious to me. 

But... since literally everyone tells me they don't see it, I do sometimes stop and wonder if maybe my mind is playing tricks on me, or if I'm blowing it out of proportion. It's just really hard to actually believe them when the puffiness feels so real every single time I look.
Do you find yourself spending a significant amount of time checking your face in the mirror or asking others for reassurance about how you look?

Yes, I do. A lot, actually. Before my work meetings or if I'm getting ready to go somewhere, I... well, I keep opening the camera preview on my phone or laptop. I'll sit there changing the angle and the lighting, just checking it. And I'm constantly fixing my hair around that left side of my face, trying to see if I can make it look better. 

I also end up retaking pictures of myself over and over. And I definitely ask my friends if I look strange. I do all of this so much that, honestly, half the time I end up making myself late, or I just get so drained from the whole process that I don't even want to go out anymore.
Aside from checking in the mirror or asking for reassurance, do you ever feel compelled to touch, pick at, or try to 'fix' the skin or features on that side of your face?

Um, no, not really. I don't find myself picking at my skin or touching it a lot. It's... it's really just the looking, and like I mentioned, moving my hair around to try and hide the shape of it. But I don't actually try to physically mess with the skin or the features themselves. I just stare at it.
